questions.question: Compare column family and graph data models of No SQL databases.
questions.solution_html: • Compare column family and graph data models of NoSQL databases./ [CO4] Column family Data is organized into rows, where each row contains a key and a set of column families. Columns are flexible and can be sparse (a row may not have all columns). Use Cases-Time-series data, high-volume logging, real-time analytics, and applications requiring extreme horizontal scaling and write-heavy operations. Excellent horizontal scalability (sharding/distribution is by row key). Graph Data Model Data is structured as a network of Nodes (entities) and Edges (relationships) with associated properties. Use cases-Social networks, recommendation engines, fraud detection, and any system where relationships are as important as the data itself. Scales well for large numbers of nodes and edges; performance depends heavily on the complexity of the traversal.

questions.question: Discuss about dirty read, nonrepeatable read and phantom problem in a transaction.
questions.solution_html: • Discuss about dirty read, nonrepeatable read and phantom problem in a transaction. / [CO3] Dirty Read (Temporary Update Problem): a. Occurs when: Transaction T1 reads a data item that has been modified by a concurrent transaction T2 , but T2 has not yet committed. b. Problem: If T2 later rolls back its changes, T1 has read a value that never officially existed in the database, leading to inconsistent results. Nonrepeatable Read: c. Occurs when: Transaction T1 reads the same data item twice. Between the two reads, a different transaction T2 updates or deletes that specific item and commits. d. Problem: T1 gets different values for the same item upon repeating its read, violating the transaction's isolation. Phantom Problem (Phantom Read): e. Occurs when: Transaction T1 executes a query (e.g., a SELECT with a WHERE clause) that retrieves a set of rows. A different transaction T2 then inserts a new row that satisfies T1 's WHERE clause and commits. f. Problem: When T1 repeats the query, it sees a new, unexpected "phantom" row, changing the set of rows retrieved

Define suitable relationships and attributes for each entity. / [CO2] Concept Notation Description Entity Type Rectangle Represents a collection of real-world objects (e.g., Student, Course). Attribute Ellipse Represents a property of an entity (e.g., Name, ID). Key Attribute Underlined Ellipse An attribute that is the Primary Key for the entity (e.g., SId ). Relationship Type Diamond Represents an association between two or more entities (e.g., TEACHES).
